title: Finite modules free at all primes are locally free on an affine cover
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $M$ be a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. If for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ the localization $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finite free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module], then there are finitely many elements $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that each localization $M_{f_i}$ is a finite free $A_{f_i}$-module. Equivalently, the quasi-coherent sheaf $\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme, lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] is finite locally free.

source.place: Tag 0GWM (algebra-lemma-finitely-presented-localization-free), together with Tag 01XZ (coherent-lemma-quasi-coherent) for finite presentation on Noetherian affines

proof.text: Because $A$ is Noetherian and $M$ is finite, $M$ is finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 0517, Noetherian finite modules are finitely presented

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the hypothesis gives that $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is finite free. Applying [lem-sc-finitely-presented-free-at-prime-principal] yields an element $f_{\mathfrak p}\notin\mathfrak p$ for which $M_{f_{\mathfrak p}}$ is finite free; thus the principal opens $D(f_{\mathfrak p})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.

The spectrum of $A$ is quasi-compact, so finitely many of these principal opens cover it. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i), their defining elements $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ generate the unit ideal. Each corresponding localization $M_{f_i}$ is finite free by construction.

source.place: Tags 00E0 and 00E8, Zariski topology and quasi-compactness of Spec

proof.text: On $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, the module sheaf $\widetilde M$ has sections $M_f$ on each principal open $D(f)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Therefore the finite principal cover above trivializes $\widetilde M$ by finite free modules, which is exactly finite local freeness.

lean.statement: theorem finite_free_at_primes_localized_cover {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (hfree : Module.freeLocus A M = Set.univ) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → A), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, Module.Free (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M) ∧ Module.Finite (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)
lean.note: The first declaration gives the affine cover in independent ring/module universes; the second states the equivalent finite locally free tilde-sheaf conclusion using the existing varying-rank predicate.
